filmIssues: The pull-back concept is right — tight on the suitcase at t=0 opening, then revealing the boy, window, sunrise and jet by t=1 — and both end frames are readable compositions.

The suitcase layer breaks coherence: at depth 0.9 with drift -0.015/0.012 and end scale 0.93 it slides down-left away from the boy across the frames, increasingly detached from the legs it should stand beside, as if rolling unattended across the floor.

By t=0.8-1 the drifting suitcase is pushed to the bottom-left corner and sits awkwardly against / slightly clipped by the frame edge, spoiling the final dwell picture compared with the plate where it rests firmly next to the boy.

Apart from the suitcase slide there is no obvious tearing, doubled edge or painted-over ghost, the light-sweep is fitting for sunrise and subtle, and the risograph grain is preserved — the fault is the layer separation, not the camera idea.

rounds.verdict: A coherent, clean pull-back ending on the full plate, but too timid and generic to publish: the suitcase-led departure reveal never really lands at the opening.
filmIssues: The pull-back is visible but timid: across the six frames the boy, window and suitcase only shrink and drift slightly, so the film reads as a plain slow zoom-out rather than a purposeful departure reveal.

The opening frame is not the claimed tight picture of the packed suitcase. At t=0 the suitcase is still small in the lower-left corner with the boy and window dominating, so the intended suitcase-to-full-scene story is not clear on either forward or reverse play.

Only the suitcase is a cut-out and it is locked at low depth with no drift, scale or entrance, so there is no layered storytelling beyond the camera move; against a plain centred move this adds little.

The subject does stay coherent — no tearing, doubled edges, halo, ghosting or awkward frame-edge clipping is visible, and the suitcase stays with the boy and floor — and the final full-plate frame is a good dwell picture. The light-sweep is subtle and fitting for sunrise, and the risograph orange/teal print style is preserved.

plan.rationale: Keep the purposeful departure reveal — open tight on the packed orange suitcase, then pull back steadily to the boy from behind, the sunrise window and the waiting jet — but lock the suitcase to the boy and floor: low depth near the background, no drift and no shrink, so boy and case stay together as one departing figure and the case never slides to or clips the frame edge. rounds.verdict: Not publishable as an 8+ film: technically coherent, but the motion as rendered is essentially a timid wide-shot zoom-out and does not deliver the planned suitcase-to-departure reveal.
filmIssues: The intended tight opening on the suitcase does not read: at t=0 the suitcase is still a small lower-left prop in a near-complete wide shot of the boy and window.
Across all six frames the pull-back is very slight and close to a plain centred zoom-out; the boy, jet, sunrise and palm trees are visible from the start, so there is no clear departure reveal.
The suitcase layer has minimum practical depth and no drift, producing almost no parallax or separation from the background during the camera move.
The light-sweep is not visibly legible in the frames, although it is thematically suitable for sunrise.
The final frame is a good full-plate dwell image, and no obvious tearing, doubled edges, haloing or ghosting is visible around the suitcase.
